Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Situation2: They notice a local festival happening nearby and casually stop to observe some of the decorations and rituals.
Story: I was walking home from work when my phone buzzed. It was Priya, my closest friend, texting, “Ugh, today was endless. Can I vent?” I knew she needed me to listen, to be there for her, like always. I started typing a reply, but just then, I heard the sound of drums and laughter. I looked up and realized the street was alive with colors—our local Hindu festival was in full swing. My family always expected me to join, to show respect, to participate in the rituals and soak in the community spirit. I could see my neighbors waving, motioning for me to come over. I felt the pull of tradition, the warmth of belonging, but Priya’s message blinked on my screen, a reminder of my promise to be a good friend. My heart raced as I stood there, torn between the comfort of my faith and the loyalty of friendship, feeling the weight of both expectations pressing in on me.
